paper.title: A general modular framework for gene set enrichment analysis
paper.citation: Ackermann M, Strimmer K. A general modular framework for gene set enrichment analysis. BMC Bioinformatics 10:47 (2009)

items.label: Table 1, methods in the literature

cause.summary: A list of published methods and their references; nothing to compute.

items.label: Fig. 1, the five modules

cause.summary: A diagram of the framework; it is the structure of the package gseamod.

items.label: Text: 3 x 5 x 6 x 3 - 9 = 261 variants

fields.name: 3 gene-level statistics x 5 transformations x 6 gene set statistics x 3 significance assessments - 9 (ES with binary)

items.note: The count leaves out the parametric significance option that Table 4 reports (only with the mean and Wilcoxon).

items.label: Table 2, gene-level statistic x transformation (mean, resampling)

assumptions.what: Each simulated data set is analysed with every combination of modules; the paper simulated 100 data sets per combination
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper's Tables 2, 3 and 4 print the same squared mod.t / mean / resampling cell, so it shared data there too. On squared statistics maxmean equals the mean, so our maxmean column repeats the mean column; the paper's differ by up to 0.04 (set 9), as separate data would.

assumptions.what: Seeds 20090203 + replicate for the data and 20090203 + 100000 + replicate for the random gene sets and label permutations (1000 of each, shared by the combinations of a replicate)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper gives no seeds. Any seed changes each rate by Monte Carlo error only; the tolerance of every field is a 99% two-proportion band for two shares of 100 (gseamod::rate_tolerance).

assumptions.what: The background genes of sets 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 are drawn at random for each set and each replicate
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper says 'selected randomly' without saying whether the draws overlap; overlaps change no expected rate.

assumptions.what: Every test is one-sided (large statistics enriched) and its p-value is the share of null statistics at or above the observed one
assumptions.sensitivity: Without transformation set 3 lies below random sets of all 600 genes (40 up-shifted genes raise their mean), so a one-sided test never calls it, as in the paper's 0.00; a two-sided test would.

assumptions.what: The binary transformation calls a gene at two-sided p <= 0.05 (t distribution for t and mod.t, Fisher's z for correlations)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper gives no cutoff. Calling genes at local fdr <= 0.2 (fdrtool) instead calls almost no gene and drops the detection rates far below the paper's (variant binary_lfdr02 in tables.json).

assumptions.what: Local fdr from fdrtool with a normal null for t and mod.t and a correlation null for correlations; the transformed score is 1 - lfdr
assumptions.sensitivity: Not varied. fdrtool is the second author's package; the paper does not say which null was used.

review.note: Review card "Table 2": Partly. 135 of 135 rates lie in the Monte Carlo band, but the binary cutoff was chosen after seeing the paper's rates; the reviewer gave no further reason on the card.

cause.summary: Every rate lies in the 99% Monte Carlo band (135 of 135), but two settings are not in the paper: the binary transformation's cutoff (two-sided p <= 0.05, chosen because a local fdr <= 0.2 rule called almost no gene) and the local fdr null. The reviewer set the verdict to partly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper's binary rule is local fdr <= 0.2
hypotheses.test: Variant binary_lfdr02 over the same 100 data sets
hypotheses.detail: Rates fall far below the paper's (set 1, mod.t: 0.13 against 0.61).

assumptions.what: Cond. FDR statistic: the mean over the set of 1 - fdr_S, with fdr_S(z) = fdr(z) (m/N) / pi_S(z), fdr from fdrtool on the untransformed statistic and pi_S from a linear logistic regression of set membership on the transformed statistic
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper names only the logistic regression. Its slope alone is a monotone function of the set's score sum, so it gives exactly the mean's p-values under resampling (variant condslope), while the paper's cond. FDR column differs from its mean column.

cause.summary: 51 of 54 rates agree. Cond. FDR misses sets 8 and 9 (0.53 and 0.84 against 0.84 and 0.99) and ES misses set 8 (0.44 against 0.65): the paper does not define its cond. FDR statistic or its ES ordering on squared scores.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cond. FDR is the slope of the logistic regression of set membership on the score
hypotheses.test: Variant condslope over the same 100 data sets
hypotheses.detail: The slope gives exactly the mean's p-values under resampling (set 8: 0.57, set 9: 0.92), not the paper's 0.84 and 0.99.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cond. FDR is the mean over the set of 1 - fdr_S (Efron's conditional fdr from that regression)
hypotheses.detail: Set 8: 0.53, set 9: 0.84 against 0.84 and 0.99.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our correlated sets are less correlated than the paper's (rho 0.8 or 0.9 instead of 0.6)
hypotheses.test: variants.json: mean and Wilcoxon with resampling at rho 0.6, 0.8, 0.9 (ES and cond. FDR were not rerun)
hypotheses.detail: The mean's set 8 stays at 0.52 to 0.57 at every rho. The ES gap is on set 8 only; cond. FDR misses sets 8 and 9; neither statistic was rerun at higher rho.

review.note: Review card "Table 5": Agrees. The one rate outside the band (set 3, parametric) is 0.050 on 400 more data sets.

cause.summary: 35 of 36 rates agree. The parametric false positive rate of set 3 is 0.13 in our 100 data sets against 0.02; on 400 more data sets it is 0.050, so the 0.13 is chance in our sample (the same data sets also give 0.12 by permutation).

hypotheses.hypothesis: globaltest 5.56's asymptotic p-value is anti-conservative for 20 samples
hypotheses.test: Set 3 on 400 more data sets (variants.json, null_set3)
hypotheses.detail: Parametric 0.050, permutation 0.045.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our 100 data sets happen to hold more large set-3 statistics than usual
hypotheses.test: The same 400 data sets; the permutation rate of our 100 data sets
hypotheses.detail: Permutation, which is exact, also gives 0.12 on our 100 data sets and 0.045 on the 400.

assumptions.what: Hotelling T2 = t' R^-1 t with R the corpcor shrinkage correlation of the data centred within each class
assumptions.sensitivity: Centring over all samples (variant hotelling_overall) or shrinking the covariance instead (hotelling_cov) moves the correlated sets; see the cause of Table 6.

cause.summary: 25 of 27 rates agree. Set 1 is found more often than in the paper (0.25 against 0.09 by resampling and 0.25 against 0.08 by restandardization): the paper does not say how its shrinkage correlation was estimated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The correlation was estimated without centring within the classes
hypotheses.test: Variant hotelling_overall over the same 100 data sets
hypotheses.detail: Set 1 falls to 0.01, but sets 2 and 7 fall to 0.60 and 0.56 against the paper's 0.92 and 1.00.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The covariance, not the correlation, was shrunk
hypotheses.detail: Set 1: 0.17, set 6: 0.11 against 0.09 and 0.25.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper's correlated sets were more correlated than 0.6
hypotheses.test: variants.json: rho 0.8 and 0.9, Hotelling with resampling
hypotheses.detail: At rho 0.8 set 1 is 0.10 (paper 0.09) but set 6 drops to 0.09 (paper 0.25); the mean's set 1 does not move (0.58).

assumptions.what: Each simulated data set is analysed with every combination of modules; the paper simulated 100 data sets per combination
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper's Tables 2, 3 and 4 print the same squared mod.t / mean / resampling cell, so it shared data there too. On squared statistics maxmean equals the mean, so our maxmean column repeats the mean column; the paper's differ by up to 0.04 (set 9), as separate data would.

assumptions.what: Seeds 20090203 + replicate for the data and 20090203 + 100000 + replicate for the random gene sets and label permutations (1000 of each, shared by the combinations of a replicate)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper gives no seeds. Any seed changes each rate by Monte Carlo error only; the tolerance of every field is a 99% two-proportion band for two shares of 100 (gseamod::rate_tolerance).

assumptions.what: The background genes of sets 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 are drawn at random for each set and each replicate
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper says 'selected randomly' without saying whether the draws overlap; overlaps change no expected rate.

assumptions.what: Every test is one-sided (large statistics enriched) and its p-value is the share of null statistics at or above the observed one
assumptions.sensitivity: Without transformation set 3 lies below random sets of all 600 genes (40 up-shifted genes raise their mean), so a one-sided test never calls it, as in the paper's 0.00; a two-sided test would.
